Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the latest MSA. Our legal team has pushed back on the mutual exclusion language for special/incidental/consequential damages — they say Acme needs a one-way carveout (i.e., Redwood remains liable for certain kinds of downstream loss) given the nature of the integration and historical concerns around availability. Attached is our annotated redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v4.docx).

Main asks:
- Make the consequential damages exclusion one-way in favor of Acme for lost revenue/lost business (their preference).
- Carve out data loss and regulatory fines for Acme as express exceptions.
- Keep caps but increase for incidents tied to Redwood platform outages.

Can we get a short call this week to align? Jordan

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: ACME redlines — recommended position

Team — forwarding Jordan's note. I drafted a compromise to present to Acme on the call. High level: avoid a blunt one-way exclusion but give Acme measurable protections via (A) a tiered cap structure tied to incident severity and (B) a narrow set of carveouts that are objective and claim-specific.

Suggested language (for negotiation) — please review and flag edits:

"Limitation of Liability; Exceptions. EXCEPT FOR (i) each party's indemnification obligations for third-party claims, (ii) a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, and (iii) willful misconduct or gross negligence, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS, LOSS OF DATA OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION (\"Excluded Damages\").

Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the avoidance of doubt and subject to the aggregate caps below, the following shall constitute permitted direct recovery (\"Permitted Direct Damages\"): (a) direct costs incurred to restore lost customer data resulting from Redwood's failure to follow its documented backup and retention procedures, and (b) reasonable incremental costs directly resulting from prolonged unavailability of the Service (measured as contiguous downtime exceeding the Service Level Agreement target by more than 24 hours).

Tiered caps (per incident / aggregate):
- Tier 1 (Operational incident): cap = 1x monthly committed spend for the affected account (per incident)
- Tier 2 (Major outage/data loss): cap = 6x monthly committed spend or $500,000, whichever is greater (per incident)
- Aggregate annual cap: 12x monthly committed spend or $1,000,000, whichever is greater

These Permitted Direct Damages provisions and Tiered caps are intended to be reciprocal, but with the following one-way carve (acceptable to Redwood): Redwood will not seek to recover consequential damages from Customer; Customer may assert Permitted Direct Damages as set forth above. The carveouts are limited and objective (data restoration tied to documented backups; prolonged downtime defined by SLA overage)."

Rationale: preserves mutual exclusion for broadly defined consequential damages while giving the customer objective remedies tied to measurable operational failures. It avoids open-ended lost profits claims and keeps our exposure bounded.

Attachment: liability_matrix_v3.xlsx (draft showing how tiers map to incident types).

Please reply with edits. I want to be ready to present this on the call with Jordan on Mon 10/18.

-Rishi

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: ACME redlines — recommended position

Rishi — good framing. Edits below (tracked here inline):

1) Narrow the Permitted Direct Damages list further: remove \"business interruption\" from Permitted Direct Damages — that tends to be a conduit for lost profits claims. Keep only (a) restoration of lost customer data caused by Redwood's failure to follow its documented backup/retention procedures, and (b) demonstrable incremental costs for emergency remediation services (e.g., third-party engineering/time-and-materials) incurred to restore the Service.

2) Clarify that the data restoration carveout applies only where Redwood's documented backups were in use and the customer timely followed Redwood's documented recovery procedures.

3) Replace the phrase \"Redwood will not seek to recover consequential damages from Customer\" with \"Neither party will seek recovery of Excluded Damages from the other, except as explicitly provided in the Permitted Direct Damages\" — preserves reciprocity and avoids a perception of a unilateral concession.

4) Tighten definitions: define \"Prolonged unavailability\" as contiguous downtime exceeding 48 hours beyond SLA overage measured from the time Redwood first acknowledges the incident.

5) Suggest adding an explicit carveout for regulatory fines only where a court or final administrative determination holds Redwood responsible for the underlying deficiency (we shouldn't accept an automatic carveout for all regulatory fines).

If you want I can mark these in the doc; otherwise looks good to present as a middle ground.

-Laura

Subject: RE: MSA redline v4 — damages carveouts (proposed compromise)

Jordan / Acme team —

Appreciate you surfacing the concern. After internal review, our legal and GTM teams put together a narrow compromise we believe protects Acme operationally while keeping our exposure bounded. Below is the text we propose to put into the MSA; we read it live on a short call if helpful.

Proposed compromise language: (please consider and let us know if this is sufficient)

"Limitation of Liability; Exceptions. EXCEPT FOR (i) each party's indemnification obligations for third-party claims, (ii) a party's material breach of its confidentiality obligations, and (iii) willful misconduct or gross negligence, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OR INTERRUPTION OF BUSINESS (\"Excluded Damages\").

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following limited remedies (\"Permitted Direct Damages\") shall be available: (a) documented, reasonable costs to restore Customer Data that were lost as a result of Redwood's failure to follow its documented backup and retention procedures, provided Customer followed Redwood's published recovery procedures in a timely manner; and (b) reasonable, documented, out-of-pocket third-party remediation costs incurred to restore the Service following a verified Redwood operational failure resulting in contiguous downtime exceeding 48 hours beyond the Service Level Agreement overage threshold (measured from Redwood's first acknowledged incident notification).

Tiered caps (per incident / aggregate):
- Tier 1 (Operational incident): cap = 1x monthly committed spend (per incident)
- Tier 2 (Major outage/data loss): cap = 6x monthly committed spend or $500,000, whichever is greater (per incident)
- Aggregate annual cap: 12x monthly committed spend or $1,000,000, whichever is greater

The Permitted Direct Damages and Tiered caps set forth above are intended to be reciprocal. For the avoidance of doubt, neither party may recover Excluded Damages from the other except as expressly provided in the Permitted Direct Damages."

Attachments: liability_matrix_v3.xlsx (high level mapping of incident types to tiers) and the ACME_MSA_redline_v4.docx with annotated suggested text.

If this is acceptable, please confirm and we will incorporate the text into the redline and proceed. If not, highlight which specific carveouts you need to keep as one-way and we can talk through the use case and documentation that would make it objective.

Best,
